The engagement

What happens on Thursdays 1 and 2

Thursday 1 of 6 — Where the money goes

You bring
Last three months of bank statements, your current price list, payroll dates.
You leave with
A twelve-week cash calendar with the tight weeks marked.
Homework

Circle the two payments you could move if next month looks like this one.

Price it

Thursday 2 of 6 — What a job really costs

You bring
Three recent jobs, invoices, material receipts, hours logged.
You leave with
A true cost per job and a price you can say out loud.
Homework

Post the new price sheet where your team sees it before Friday.

Price it

Thursdays 3 and 4 — People and process

Thursday 3 of 6 — Who does what

You bring
Your current org chart (even if it is just names on a napkin).
You leave with
Written roles and the description of the next hire.
Homework

Ask one person to own a task they have been doing without being asked.

Price it

Thursday 4 of 6 — The jobs only you know

You bring
The thing that stops when you take a week off.
You leave with
Steps someone else can follow, with photos.
Homework

Watch someone else do it from the binder, not from memory.

Price it

Thursdays 5 and 6 — Growth and the plan

Thursday 5 of 6 — What to stop paying for

You bring
Last year's marketing spend, referral sources, lost leads.
You leave with
One page: who you want more of, where they look, what to cut.
Homework

Cancel one channel that has not earned its keep in six months.

Price it

Thursday 6 of 6 — The written plan

You bring
The five pages from the last five weeks.
You leave with
A bound plan with numbers, dates and the next hire described.
Homework

Hand it to someone who needs to believe it.

Price it

Common questions

What if the first Thursday is not useful?

If the first session isn't useful to you, you don't pay for it.

Do you work with businesses outside Northampton?

In person across Florence, Easthampton, Amherst, Hadley, Hatfield, Williamsburg and Holyoke; by video anywhere in Massachusetts.

Can I stop after any session?

Yes. You keep every page we wrote together.

From owners in the Valley

What they walked away with

4.9 out of 5 (64 reviews) Sample review

We met after I closed the bookshop, six Thursdays in a row, at the table in the back. Each time I went home with one page and one thing to do. By the fifth week I had stopped dreading the mail.

Hollis B., Northampton Six-session business plan Sample review

The cash calendar showed me the March gap in January. I moved a supplier payment and asked two wholesale accounts to pay on delivery. Payroll cleared the whole winter.

Ines V., Florence Cash flow planning Sample review

I had not changed my prices since I opened the bike shop. Ruth sat with my old invoices and worked out what a tune-up really costs me. I raised it, posted the new sheet, and nobody blinked.

Teddy K., Easthampton Pricing review Sample review

Our farm stand went year-round and suddenly we had eight people and no idea who was in charge of what. We came out with three written roles and a schedule my sister and I both agreed to.

Marguerite D., Hadley Hiring & team roles Sample review
